02.summary: Six hand-cranked noise machines, one for each family of noise, that you play by dragging their pitch up and down.

06.summary: A grid of coloured rectangles you can hear: across is time, up is pitch, and each colour is an instrument.

11.summary: A film strip of short sound shots, where the biggest music happens in the cuts between them.

14.summary: A walker drifts through a map of a city; each district has its own sound and the city’s pull picks the route.

22.summary: A chord machine where the rules of tuning are yours to edit: how many notes in the octave and how the overtones stretch.

32.summary: Build a brand-new sound from nothing, one harmonic at a time, then let it flower through your own sample.

42.summary: A crowd of amateur players, each with a little tune of their own, who come and go as you add them or send them home.

43.summary: A rickety machine of meshing gears; every tooth strikes a note, so the gear ratios turn into polyrhythms.

47.summary: Gliding sirens drive great masses of sound; drag them through space and listen to them collide or push apart.

49.summary: A drum machine made of letters: type a line and every character becomes a sung vowel or a percussive sound.

50.summary: One slider takes the same recording from plain fact to something slowed, stylised and staged.

54.summary: Set a musical process going and listen to it run, as copies of one pattern drift apart, fill in or stretch out.

57.summary: Play a whole live set from one pad sampler: chop a phrase across sixteen pads, record patterns and build to a drop.

58.summary: Tap and each note blooms, returns every cycle a little quieter, and carries on by itself when you stop.

59.summary: Four virtual turntables: cut any sound into short sound objects, then loop, slow, reverse and trim them.

61.summary: Objects send out coloured rays that bounce off the edges, and music happens only where the rays cross.

63.summary: Two short melodies of different lengths feed a long tape-delay loop, so every note returns quieter and darker for minutes.

66.summary: A grid sequencer of small shapes inside squares; mirror, invert and multiply the grid to make endless variations.

67.summary: Cut a vocal into lines, reorder them, stack loops on house or garage drums and add each tune to an ever-growing folder.

69.summary: A diamond of pure tuning ratios you can walk through, pivoting between chords built up and chords built down.

70.summary: Birds cut their sounds into syllables and sing them through grammars you can edit, as a dawn chorus builds.

74.summary: The old five-step method for learning counterpoint, as a machine that writes a fresh second line against a fixed tune.

75.summary: A loop that stays the same while what it plays keeps changing, like a river whose water is never the same twice.

76.summary: A pop-song factory driven by eleven giant word faders, from Transient to Big business.

78.summary: A map of a marsh you walk across, where distance decides what you hear and old sounds are composted into new ones.

81.summary: Paint gestures on four layers without stopping to think, and the gestures play.

55.summary: Every bird in a murmuration is a sound: its height sets the pitch and its speed sets the level, and no bird leads.
